result.journal: International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications
result.keywords: SummaryThis paper presents a fictional nonisolated dual-input dc-dc converter topology designed for hybrid energy systems and sensitive loads. The proposed converter combines soft-switching operation with continuous input current and reduced input current ripple, while supporting boost, buck, and buck-boost modes. The structure uses a compact switch count to interface multiple voltage sources and is analyzed for steady-state operation, voltage stress, and current relationships. Simulation and prototype-style validation are described for the theoretical model, with emphasis on efficiency, mode transition, and applicability to renewable and storage-integrated power networks.
result.title: A hybrid nonisolated dual-input soft-switching dc-dc converter for ripple-reduced multiport energy systems
